Chief_Complaint.content: 3-day history of watery diarrhea occurring approximately 6–7 times per day
Left lower quadrant crampy intermittent abdominal pain

History_of_Present_Illness.content: 3-day history of watery diarrhea occurring approximately 6–7 times per day
Left lower quadrant crampy intermittent abdominal pain
Initial vomiting on day 1 of illness with no vomiting since
Felt feverish early in the illness but currently afebrile
Currently tolerating fluids such as soups and smoothies
Possible trigger is Chinese takeaway consumed 4 days ago

History_of_Present_Illness.content: No similar illness in family except one child who vomited only
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: no similar illness in family (one child vomited only)

Medications.content: Oral rehydration solution such as Dioralyte to be taken as desired
Paracetamol 1 g every 6 hours as needed for fever or aches, maximum 4 g in 24 hours
Medications.source_text: Paracetamol 1 g q6h PRN fever/aches (max 4 g/24 h)

Social_and_Family_History.content: Lives with wife and two children

Assessment.content: Acute gastroenteritis, likely viral, possibly triggered by recent takeaway, currently improving but still symptomatic
Assessment.source_text: Acute gastroenteritis – likely viral; triggered by recent takeaway; currently improving but still symptomatic

Plan_of_Care.content: Oral rehydration with solutions such as Dioralyte as desired
Paracetamol 1 g every 6 hours as needed for fever or aches, maximum 4 g in 24 hours
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Paracetamol 1 g q6h PRN fever/aches (max 4 g/24 h)

Plan_of_Care.content: Rest and take 2–3 days off work
Return to clinic or seek review if no improvement in 3–4 days, if symptoms worsen, or if blood appears in stool or vomit
Plan_of_Care.source_text: RTC/seek review if no improvement 3–4 d, worsening sx, or blood in stool/vomit
